description: Mission: possible here to explore deep space.
summary:
In Mission: Possible, one needs to design their own space mission. First, they select their destination (Earth orbit, Moon, or Mars). Then, they select the rocket, engine, fuel type, solar panels, instruments, and radio. All choices affect delta-v, power, data return, and cost in real time. Next, they launch the flight and watch its progress and crew discussions and some random events on the way.

This game deals with the challenge by introducing the player into the reality of the mission. More powerful rockets are more expensive, more instruments consume more power, and more fuel reduces space for experiments. The game also uses NASA data such as distance to Mars from the Sun, intensity of the sunlight, and delay of the signals.

It is important since few people understand why the missions fail or succeed. If your mission fails, you will learn an interesting fact from NASA (e.g., a mistake in the units of the Mars Climate Orbiter). If it succeeds, you will find out what was discovered. Anyone can learn space engineering by playing.
details:
What it does and how it works

Mission: Possible is a space mission design game played in a browser window. The player selects their destination and builds a mission using a launcher, engine, fuel tanks, solar panel, instruments, and communication system. Readouts are automatically updated at every selection, giving delta-v, power, data rate, and budget.

After launching a mission, the game simulates the process through five stages: pad, ascent, orbit, deep space, and arrival. Every rocket has its own unique staging (the heavy rocket drops two side boosters). A cast of fictionalized NASA-like characters gives comments during the game. The random events, such as solar particle storms or computer resets, force the player to take action. The game gives scores on how much science was gathered, budget left, and mission success.

The simulation is based on the rocket equation for fuel and delta-v and the inverse square law for solar energy, eclipses, radiation, light-time delay, and downlink capacity. A seeded random number generator gives the ability to repeat the same mission with identical luck.

Benefits

The player feels mission trade-offs instead of reading about them. More powerful rockets cost more, more instruments need more power, and more fuel
